request: a dark doom fusion in Darbari, key of D, teental, 120 bpm

seed_riff.reasoning: A 16-matra doom cycle built on Darbari's roots: low Sa sustain with palm-muted chugs, moving through g, R, m, P, and komal d-n turnaround sliding back into sam.

phrase_plan.climax_and_sam: peaks on komal dha and ni at matras 9-10 before resolving to home Sa and landing on vadi Re at the sam

energy_arc:
alaap: Spooky, atmospheric unmetered exposition over the low D drone.
mukhada: Heavy mid-tempo doom entrance with monolithic power chords and singing sitar.
manjha: Somber, cavernous pull down into the mandra register.
mukhada: Re-establishment of the heavy groove with increased drum intensity.
breakdown: Crushing, low-end rhythmic pulverization with lead resting.
antara: High-register ascent lifting the emotional weight into taar Sa.
taan_long: Maximum virtuosic peak driven by relentless double-kick doom rhythm.
mukhada: Triumphant, weighted return of the central hook at full band power.
outro: Slow decaying doom chords trailing into the eternal tanpura.

rhythm_section.reasoning: Darbari Kanada doom arrangement plan: The home key is D (S), held low and immense. The mukhada establishes a heavy half-time doom pattern moving from S to R and P, anchoring the sitar's hook with resonant sustained chords and palm-muted 8th chugs, ending with a crushing 16th-note turnaround into sam. The manjha descends deeply into the mandra saptak (dwelling on d and P), where the rhythm section pulls back into sparse, reverberant modal drones. Section 3 returns to the mukhada chord pattern verbatim. Section 4 breakdown unleashes the composers' main riff in full crushing weight. In Section 5 (antara), the guitar climbs (+1) to match the sitar's ascent into taar Sa, ringing sparse 4-beat chords on m and P without muddy chugs. Section 6 (taan_long) locks into a driven home-pedal doom engine at full momentum. Section 7 reprises the mukhada hook. Section 8 outro lets decaying S and mandra power chords fade under the dying oscillation of the sitar.

parts.role: Mukhada statement: Monolithic half-time doom groove supporting sitar's opening theme with heavy sustain and 16th-note sam turnaround.
Manjha: Sparse, dark ringing chords shifting down to mandra d and P, letting sitar's low gamaks breathe in vast reverb.
Mukhada return: Identical chord and riff structure to section 1 reinforcing the central hook.
Breakdown: Full crushing realization of the main riff while sitar rests, driving maximum low-end doom pulverization.
Antara: Guitars shift up an octave (+1) with sparse ringing power chords on m and P, tracking sitar's ascent into taar Sa.
Taan long: Relentless driving rhythm on home pedal S to propel virtuosic gamak cascades toward the climax.
Final mukhada: Exact return of the crushing theme at full peak intensity.
Outro: Decaying, spacious doom chords trailing off into the eternal low D drone.
